senses.definition: difficult to understand; obscure
senses.example: The lecture on string theory was too abstruse for most of the audience.

senses.definition: an award or privilege granted as a special honor or in acknowledgment of merit
senses.example: The film won every major accolade of the year.

senses.definition: to make something bad or unsatisfactory better
senses.example: The new policy aims to ameliorate conditions in the prisons.

senses.definition: a person or thing that is the direct opposite of someone or something else
senses.example: Her calm was the antithesis of her brother's panic.

senses.definition: extreme greed for wealth or material gain
senses.example: His avarice drove him to cheat his own family.

senses.definition: a statement or proposition regarded as being established, accepted or self-evidently true
senses.example: It is an axiom of business that cash is king.

senses.definition: rough and bad-mannered; coarse
senses.example: His boorish behavior at dinner embarrassed his hosts.

senses.definition: to persuade an unwilling person to do something by using force or threats
senses.example: The suspect claimed he had been coerced into confessing.

senses.definition: to express or feel sympathy or pity
senses.example: Friends called to commiserate with her after the loss.

senses.definition: an extensive fire which destroys a great deal of land or property
senses.example: The conflagration destroyed half of the old town.

senses.definition: to do something that one considers to be below one's dignity
senses.example: She didn't even deign to reply to my letter.

senses.definition: to raise doubts or objections or show reluctance
senses.example: When asked to sign, she demurred.

senses.definition: spread out over a large area; not concentrated
senses.example: The diffuse light of the overcast sky cast no shadows.

senses.definition: lacking clarity or conciseness
senses.example: The essay was so diffuse that its argument got lost.

senses.definition: to spread over a wide area or among a large number of people
senses.example: The idea diffused quickly through the scientific community.

senses.definition: a person who cultivates an area of interest without real commitment or knowledge
senses.example: He was a dilettante who dabbled in painting, poetry and music.

senses.definition: to harm the good reputation of someone
senses.example: The scandal discredited the entire administration.

senses.definition: to cause an idea or evidence to seem false or unreliable
senses.example: New findings discredited the old theory.

senses.definition: to swell or cause to swell because of pressure from inside
senses.example: The starving child's belly was distended.

senses.definition: cheerful and full of energy
senses.example: The ebullient host greeted every guest by name.

senses.definition: to instruct or improve someone morally or intellectually
senses.example: The museum aims to edify as well as entertain.

senses.definition: believing in or based on the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities
senses.example: The cooperative was run on egalitarian lines.

senses.definition: to set free, especially from legal, social or political restrictions
senses.example: The law emancipated thousands of enslaved people.

senses.definition: to irritate intensely; to infuriate
senses.example: The endless delays exasperated the passengers.

senses.definition: to strongly encourage or urge someone to do something
senses.example: The general exhorted his troops to hold the line.

senses.definition: to analyze and develop an idea or principle in detail
senses.example: The professor spent an hour explicating a single poem.

senses.definition: to display exaggerated flattery or affection, especially to gain favor
senses.example: The courtiers fawned over the young king.

senses.definition: lacking initiative or strength of character; irresponsible
senses.example: Her feckless brother never held a job for more than a month.

senses.definition: irritable and quarrelsome
senses.example: The tired children grew fractious.

senses.definition: (of an organization) difficult to control; unruly
senses.example: The fractious coalition collapsed within a year.

senses.definition: to shock or excite someone into taking action
senses.example: The disaster galvanized volunteers across the country.

senses.definition: to coat iron or steel with a protective layer of zinc
senses.example: The bucket was galvanized to stop it from rusting.

senses.definition: silly; stupid
senses.example: The show was full of inane chatter.

senses.definition: to suggest or hint something bad in an indirect and unpleasant way
senses.example: Are you insinuating that I lied?

senses.definition: to maneuver oneself into a favorable position by subtle manipulation
senses.example: He insinuated himself into the director's inner circle.

senses.definition: not telling the truth; lying
senses.example: The report was full of mendacious claims.

senses.definition: a wrong or inaccurate name or designation
senses.example: "Koala bear" is a misnomer, since koalas are not bears.

senses.definition: to remove a need or difficulty
senses.example: The new bridge obviates the need for a ferry.

senses.definition: assertive of authority in an annoyingly domineering way, especially with regard to trivial matters
senses.example: An officious guard insisted on searching every bag twice.

senses.definition: having a ready insight into and understanding of things
senses.example: A perspicacious editor saw the novel's potential at once.

senses.definition: slow and clumsy because of great weight
senses.example: The elephant moved with ponderous steps.

senses.definition: dull, laborious or excessively solemn
senses.example: The lecture was ponderous and hard to follow.

senses.definition: to increase rapidly in numbers; to multiply
senses.example: Coffee shops have proliferated in the city center.

senses.definition: the state or quality of conforming to conventionally accepted standards of behavior or morals
senses.example: She was a stickler for propriety.

senses.definition: childishly silly and immature
senses.example: The jokes were puerile and offensive.

senses.definition: to put something right; to correct
senses.example: The company promised to rectify the error.

senses.definition: optimistic or positive, especially in an apparently bad or difficult situation
senses.example: She remained sanguine about her chances of recovery.

words.note: Sanguine comes from the Latin for blood but means cheerfully optimistic.

senses.definition: grimly mocking or cynical
senses.example: He gave a sardonic laugh when he heard the news.

senses.definition: witheringly scornful; severely critical
senses.example: The report was a scathing indictment of the management.

senses.definition: having or showing an excessive willingness to serve or please others
senses.example: The waiter's servile manner made the guests uncomfortable.

senses.definition: comfort or consolation in a time of distress or sadness
senses.example: She found solace in music after her mother's death.

senses.definition: a mark of disgrace associated with a particular circumstance, quality or person
senses.example: The campaign aims to reduce the stigma of mental illness.

senses.definition: to prevent or hinder the progress of
senses.example: The investigation was stymied by a lack of witnesses.

senses.definition: to attempt to sell something, typically by pestering people in an aggressive or bold manner
senses.example: Street vendors touted cheap watches to tourists.

senses.definition: to promote or praise something insistently
senses.example: The diet was touted as a miracle cure.

senses.definition: to lessen the effectiveness, power or ability of, especially gradually or insidiously
senses.example: The scandal undermined public trust in the agency.

senses.definition: filled with bitter criticism or malice
senses.example: The film received vitriolic reviews.

senses.definition: playfully quaint or fanciful, especially in an appealing and amusing way
senses.example: The children's book has whimsical illustrations.
